title: Quantum resource redistribution drives spectral splits in dense neutrino gases
summary: Whether a quantum many-body system can be efficiently simulated hinges not only on its size but also on how quantum resources are organized within it. We characterize the quantum resource landscape of collective neutrino oscillations using entanglement entropy, non-local magic, and matrix product state bond dimension. Using tensor network simulations of neutrinos in the two-flavor sector, we demonstrate that spectral splits--sharp energy-dependent flavor swaps--emerge precisely where entanglement entropy is maximized and non-local magic is minimized locally.
